elements.element: Customer pays no liquidated damages or penalties.
elements.evidence: New Section 14.2.11 does not eliminate PB-payable liquidated amounts; it expressly characterises the Development Cost-based termination payments as "a liquidated amount" and converts them into "a single early-termination fee" capped at three times average monthly Development Costs. A capped liquidated fee remains a Customer-payable liquidated amount, and the retained 14.2.1-14.2.10 payment formulas are superseded rather than deleted, so the preferred no-LD outcome is not achieved.

elements.element: Any Customer-payable liquidated amount is only an early-termination fee.
elements.evidence: 14.2.11 sweeps in "each amount payable by PB under Sections 14.2.1 through 14.2.10 that is calculated by reference to Development Costs (including interest thereon and any such amount expressed as consideration for purchasing the Trial Data Package)", deems each a liquidated amount, and provides it "is payable solely as a single early-termination fee". The purchase-price framing of the Trial Data Package and the 25% interest in 14.2.10 are expressly captured, so no Development Cost-based liquidated amount escapes the recharacterisation; Approval Payments/Buy-Out Payments are commercial consideration under ARTICLE 6, not liquidated amounts.

elements.element: The early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: The fee is "not exceeding three (3) times the average monthly Development Costs paid or incurred during the twelve (12) months preceding the effective date of termination" - a three-month multiple of the only recurring monetary run-rate in this funding agreement (PB pays no recurring subscription/service fee; Development Costs, which include the SFJ Interim Management Fee and PB Costs, are the run-rate analogue). The multiple is three, computed on a trailing twelve-month average, so the cap is computable and does not exceed the three-month threshold.

elements.element: The early-termination fee is the sole liquidated amount payable by Customer.
elements.evidence: Closing words: "which fee is the sole liquidated amount payable by PB under this Agreement", reinforced by "Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in this Agreement" and by the express statement that the 14.2.1-14.2.10 amounts are "superseded by this Section 14.2.11". The exclusivity statement is Agreement-wide, not limited to Article 14.

reasons: Fallback is complete: all three fallback elements are met in operative language (single early-termination fee, three-month cap, sole liquidated amount), so the redline is position-complete at the fallback level. Preferred is not met and should be offered as the opening ask - the clean preferred fix is to delete the Development Cost multiples in 14.2.1, 14.2.2, 14.2.5.2, 14.2.6, 14.2.7, 14.2.8.1, 14.2.9 and 14.2.10 outright rather than cap them.

Minimality holds: the change is a single concise insertion (14.2.11) with no deletions elsewhere, no survival tail, no at-own-expense or procedural boilerplate, and no new requirement outside the LD checklist. The 'notwithstanding' override is narrower in practice than surgically rewriting eight retained subsections, and scoping it to Development Cost-based amounts is what preserves the ARTICLE 6 Approval Payments, Buy-Out Payment and Section 6.2 adjustment mechanics verbatim. The parenthetical on interest and Trial Data Package consideration is necessary to stop 14.2.10 and the purchase-price framing escaping the cap, so it is not an extra.

Intent is preserved: the retained 300%/150%/100% and cost-plus-25% sentences are expressly superseded rather than left in silent conflict, Section 6.4 default interest, the mutual right to pursue unliquidated damages at law, and all termination triggers/notice periods survive unchanged; no cross-reference is left dangling and no term is left undefined ('Development Costs' and 'Trial Data Package' are both defined).

Base-substitution caution to flag in the cover note (not a defect requiring repair): the cap is measured against Development Costs incurred by SFJ rather than 'fees' paid by PB, because this Agreement contains no recurring Customer-paid fee. If SFJ pushes back, be ready to fix the base to a stated dollar figure equal to three months of the then-current Development Cost budget to avoid argument about which costs enter the average.

Optional hardening: for a termination occurring within the first twelve months, the twelve-month lookback averages in pre-Effective Date months of zero cost (a result favourable to PB but likely to be challenged). Consider 'the twelve (12) months (or, if shorter, the period since the Effective Date) preceding the effective date of termination' only if SFJ raises it - adding it unprompted is unnecessary.
